items.name: use-reduced-motion
items.title: useReducedMotion
items.description: True when the visitor has asked the system for less motion.

a11y.text: Returns true while the system asks for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and re-renders when that setting changes. It returns false on the server.

items.name: use-carousel-engine
items.title: useCarouselEngine
items.description: Drag with momentum, trackpad scrolling, snapping and eased glides for a carousel; hands you each frame to draw.

a11y.text: The hook binds no key handlers. Keys and buttons move the carousel through go(index) and move(by), which the component wires up. The wheel handler only reacts to sideways wheel and trackpad swipes, or Shift with the wheel, on axis x; a vertical wheel is left to the page.
Under reduced motion every move jumps to its slide instead of gliding, and the speed passed to onFrame stays 0.
A drag ends with a click on whatever was under the pointer. The bound onClickCapture swallows that one click.

items.name: use-gl-stage
items.title: useGlStage
items.description: Runs a WebGL scene in a canvas: context lifecycle, pixel cap, live theme colours, a frame loop only on screen, and a texture atlas for pictures.

a11y.text: The canvas it creates is aria-hidden. The alt text on each GlImage is for the component to expose; the canvas itself is hidden from screen readers.
With animate on, the frame loop runs only while the stage is on screen, and never under reduced motion. Without a loop the stage draws still frames at 4 seconds of animation time.
Without WebGL, or after the GPU drops the context, status becomes failed so the component can show its fallback.

items.name: prompt-input
items.title: Prompt input
items.description: A chat input that grows with the text, takes files, and turns into a stop button while the agent writes. With `halo`, a band of primary light runs round the border while there is something to send.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Called with the trimmed text and the attached files.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Called when the visitor presses stop while a reply is being written.

props.name: busy
props.description: True while a reply is being written. The send button turns into a stop button.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder in the text field.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the text field.

props.name: accept
props.description: Lets the visitor attach files. The value is passed to the file input's accept.

props.name: footer
props.description: Optional choices next to the buttons, e.g. a model picker.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: How many lines the field grows to before it scrolls.

props.name: halo
props.description: Lights the border while there is something to send: a band of primary light runs round the ring. Off by default.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the form.

a11y.text: Enter sends and Shift+Enter makes a new line. Enter never sends while an IME is composing. After a send, focus goes back to the text field. Attach, remove, send and stop are native buttons.

The textarea is named by label (default Message) and described by a screen-reader-only hint: Enter sends. Shift and Enter makes a new line. Attach files, Send, Stop and each Remove <file name> button carry an aria-label, and their icons are aria-hidden. Attached files sit in a list labelled Attached files. The file input is aria-hidden and out of the tab order. Attach files shows only with accept. Send is disabled until there is text or a file.
With halo on, under reduced motion the ring stops spinning and stays at a fixed angle, and its fades and the arrow's shift have no transition. The buttons scale on press without a transition.
In forced colors mode the frame becomes a real border and the focus ring a real outline, because box-shadow is dropped there.

items.name: tool-approval
items.title: Tool approval
items.description: Asks the person before the agent runs a tool, with the arguments in full and a clear mark on risky calls.

props.name: tool
props.description: The tool the agent wants to call, e.g. "send_email".

props.name: summary
props.description: One sentence in plain words about what will happen.

props.name: args
props.description: The arguments, shown as JSON so nothing is hidden.

props.name: risky
props.description: Mark a call that changes something outside the app.

props.name: state
props.description: Controlled state. Leave it out and the card keeps its own.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Called when the person approves the call.

props.name: onDeny
props.description: Called when the person denies the call.

props.name: labels
props.type: { name?: string; wants?: string; arguments?: string; deny?: string; approve?: string; approveRisky?: string; approved?: string; denied?: string }
props.description: Visible text and screen reader text; defaults to English. `name` comes before the tool name in the card's accessible name.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

a11y.text: Deny and Approve are native buttons, and Arguments is a native details element, so Tab, Enter and Space work without custom handlers. After a choice the buttons leave the card, so focus moves to the card itself.

The card is a section labelled by labels.name and the tool, Approve <tool> by default. A hidden status paragraph is always in the page and is filled when you choose, so the approved or denied text is announced once. The visible result is aria-hidden to avoid a double reading, and no button sits inside a live region. The shield and check icons are aria-hidden. A risky call changes the button text to Approve anyway, not only its colour.
Under reduced motion the chevron turn, the colour transitions and the press scale on the buttons are off.

items.name: agent-activity
items.title: Agent activity
items.description: The agent's steps as a list: waiting, running, done or failed, with timings.

props.name: steps
props.description: The steps, in order, each with an id, a label and a status.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the card and name of the section.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

a11y.text: The card is a section labelled by title, with the steps in an ordered list. Each step label is followed by a screen-reader-only status: waiting, in progress, done or failed. A screen-reader-only polite live region announces only the step in progress, or All steps done, so the reader is not flooded. Icons and the connector line are aria-hidden.
The spinner on a running step stops under reduced motion.

items.name: streaming-response
items.title: Streaming response
items.description: Shows a reply as it is written. New words fade in and a caret marks the end.

props.name: text
props.description: The text so far. Append to it as tokens arrive.

props.name: streaming
props.description: True while more text is coming. Shows the caret.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer element.

a11y.text: The container is a polite live region (aria-live polite, relevant additions and text), so new words are read as they arrive without interrupting. It sets aria-busy while streaming is true. The caret is aria-hidden. Words are plain text in spans, and paragraphs are split on blank lines.
Under reduced motion the words appear without fading and the caret does not blink.

items.name: reasoning
items.title: Reasoning
items.description: The model's thinking, folded away. Open while it thinks, closed when the answer starts.

props.name: children
props.description: The model's reasoning so far. Plain text or your own markup.

props.name: streaming
props.description: True while the model is still thinking.

props.name: ms
props.description: How long the thinking took, in milliseconds. Shown once it is done.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Start open. By default it is open while streaming and closes when done.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer element.

a11y.text: The header is a native button, so Tab, Enter and Space toggle it. Once the reader has toggled it, their choice stands, even when streaming changes.

The button sets aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the content, which is hidden while closed. Its label reads Thinking while streaming, Thought for N seconds when ms is given, otherwise Reasoning. The icons are aria-hidden.
Under reduced motion the pulsing brain icon, the chevron turn and the fade-in of the opened content are off.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code block
items.description: Code with a file name and a copy button. Bring your own highlighting, or none.

props.name: code
props.description: The code as text. This is what the copy button copies.

props.name: language
props.description: Shown in the header, e.g. "tsx" or "bash".

props.name: filename
props.description: Shown in the header instead of the language, e.g. "src/app.tsx".

props.name: children
props.description: Already highlighted markup (from Shiki or similar). Without it the plain code is shown.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Number the lines.

props.name: labels
props.type: { copy?: string; copied?: string; code?: string }
props.description: Visible text and screen reader text. Keys: `copy`, `copied` and `code` (the header and region name when there is no filename or language).

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer figure.

a11y.text: The copy button is a native button. The code area is a scrollable pre with tabIndex 0, so it can be focused and scrolled with the keyboard.

The block is a figure with the file name, else the language, else Code as its caption. The code area is a region with that same name, so a focused scroll area is announced with a name. The button text lives in an aria-live polite span, so Copy becomes Copied, which resets after 1.8 seconds. The words come from labels (copy, copied, code). Line numbers are aria-hidden and unselectable. If the clipboard is blocked, nothing changes and the code can still be selected by hand.
Under reduced motion the colour transition on the copy button is off.

items.name: sources
items.title: Sources
items.description: Numbered citations after a claim and the list of sources they point to.

props.name: sources
props.description: The sources, listed in order and numbered from 1.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the list and name of the section.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

a11y.text: Citation is an anchor to #source-N, so Tab and Enter jump to the matching row in the list. Each source is a link with a 44 px minimum height.

The visible number in a Citation is aria-hidden; screen readers get Source N: title. The list is a section labelled by title with an ordered list, and every link adds a screen-reader-only (opens in a new tab). External links use target _blank with rel noreferrer. The row you jump to gets the :target background.

items.name: file-diff
items.title: File diff
items.description: A change to one file as a coding agent proposes it, from a unified diff.

props.name: filename
props.description: The file the change is in.

props.name: diff
props.description: A unified diff, as `git diff` writes it. Header lines (diff, index, ---, +++) are skipped.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer figure.

a11y.text: The diff area is a scrollable region with tabIndex 0, so it takes focus and scrolls with the arrow keys.

The scroll area has role region labelled Changes in <filename>, and the lines are table rows. The + or − sign is aria-hidden and replaced by a screen-reader-only added or removed. The counts read as N lines added, N removed. Line numbers are unselectable. Hunk lines span all columns. Added and removed lines differ by sign and text, not only by colour.

items.name: number-ticker
items.title: Number ticker
items.description: Counts up to a number when it scrolls into view. Screen readers hear only the final number.

props.name: value
props.description: The number it counts to. A new value counts on from the one shown.

props.name: from
props.description: Where the count starts the first time.

props.name: duration
props.description: Milliseconds for one count.

props.name: locale
props.description: Passed to Intl.NumberFormat, e.g. "da-DK". Defaults to the browser's language.

props.name: format
props.description: Intl.NumberFormat options, e.g. a currency or a number of decimals.

props.name: startOnView
props.description: Start counting first when the number scrolls into view.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer span.

a11y.text: Screen readers get the final value once, in a screen-reader-only span. The counting digits are aria-hidden, so the steps on the way are not read.
Under reduced motion the final number shows at once, even before it is in view. Otherwise it counts when it is 40% in view, unless startOnView is false.

items.name: blur-fade
items.title: Blur fade
items.description: Fades an element up out of a soft blur the first time it enters the view.

props.name: children
props.description: The content that fades in.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds. Use small steps (40 to 80 ms) to stagger a group.

props.name: offset
props.description: How far it rises, in pixels.

props.name: immediate
props.description: Show at once instead of waiting for the element to scroll into view.

props.name: as
props.description: The element it renders as.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the rendered element.

a11y.text: Under reduced motion the element is fully visible from the start, with no rise, blur or transition.
Pure presentation: it renders its children in a div, section, li or span (as) and adds no roles or labels.

items.name: highlighter
items.title: Highlighter
items.description: A marker stroke draws behind a phrase the first time it scrolls into view.

props.name: children
props.description: The text to mark.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds after the phrase enters the view.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the mark element.

a11y.text: The phrase is a native mark element, and its text is always in the DOM in full. The stroke is only a background image.
Under reduced motion the stroke is already fully drawn, with no transition.

items.name: text-reveal
items.title: Text reveal
items.description: Words go from faint to full as the reader scrolls through a paragraph.

props.name: children
props.description: Plain text. Each word lights up as the paragraph scrolls past.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the paragraph.

a11y.text: The whole text is always in the DOM as a plain paragraph, with each word in a span, so screen readers read it normally. Nothing is hidden or relabelled.
Under reduced motion every word is at full strength from the start, the colour transition is off and the scroll listener is not attached.
Words that are not yet lit sit at 50% opacity, which keeps the contrast needed for large text in both the light and the dark theme. Use it on large type only.

items.name: spotlight-card
items.title: Spotlight card
items.description: A card with a soft light that follows the mouse pointer.

props.name: size
props.description: Radius of the light in pixels.

a11y.text: A plain div with no interactive parts. The light is a decorative span that is aria-hidden and ignores pointer events.
The light follows a mouse pointer only. Under reduced motion the span is hidden (motion-reduce:hidden) and the card stays plain. Only a mouse pointer moves the light.

items.name: marquee
items.title: Marquee
items.description: Items scroll sideways in an endless loop and pause on hover or focus. Static under reduced motion.

props.name: children
props.description: The items that scroll. Rendered twice for a seamless loop.

props.name: duration
props.description: Seconds for one full loop.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between items in pixels.

props.name: reverse
props.description: Scrolls the other way.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the region, e.g. "Customers".

props.name: labels
props.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the pause button, with English defaults: `pause` while the strip moves, `play` while it is paused.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer region, which holds the strip and the pause button.

a11y.text: A visible 44 pixel Pause and Play button, placed after the loop in tab order, stops and starts the scrolling. The loop also pauses while the pointer is over it or focus is inside it. The second copy of the items is inert and aria-hidden, so Tab never visits it twice.

The container is a region named by label, which is required (for example Customers). The pause button is named by labels (Pause, Play) and its name changes with the state. Only the first copy of the items is exposed to screen readers.
Under reduced motion the loop stops, the second copy is hidden, the edge fade is removed, the items wrap onto lines and the pause button is hidden because nothing moves.

items.name: dot-pattern
items.title: Dot pattern
items.description: A quiet dot grid behind content, drawn with CSS only.

props.name: spacing
props.description: Distance between dots in pixels.

props.name: vignette
props.description: Fade the dots out towards the edges.

a11y.text: Decorative only, with no interactive parts. The dots are a CSS background; the vignette span (vignette, default true) is aria-hidden.

items.name: shimmer-button
items.title: Shimmer button
items.description: A primary button with a slow sheen, and an optional lean towards the pointer.

props.name: magnetic
props.description: Lean a few pixels towards the pointer.

a11y.text: A native button, so Tab, Enter and Space work as usual. It accepts all button attributes and has a minimum height of 44 px.
The shimmer is an aria-hidden span, so only the button label is read. A disabled button is dimmed.
The shimmer span is hidden under reduced motion. The magnetic lean is skipped under reduced motion and for any pointer that is not a mouse. The press scale has no transition under reduced motion.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: Short messages that stack in a corner and leave on their own. Call toast() from anywhere.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the fixed region that holds the toasts.

props.name: labels
props.description: Screen reader text with English defaults. Keys: `notifications`, `close`, `success` and `error`.

a11y.text: Close and the optional action are native buttons. The auto-dismiss timer pauses while the pointer is over a toast and while focus is inside it, and the Infinity duration keeps a toast until it is closed. An action runs its handler and then dismisses the toast.

Toasts sit in a section labelled Notifications, in an ordered list that is not itself live. Two hidden regions are always in the page: a polite status for success and info toasts, and an alert for errors, so errors are read at once. Only toasts added after the page loaded are announced, as the tone word, the title and the description. Each toast also carries the tone as hidden text before the title (Success or Error). The words come from labels (notifications, close, success, error). The close button is labelled Close, and the icons are aria-hidden. At most four toasts are kept.
Under reduced motion the enter and leave animations are off. A dismissed toast is removed 200 ms later.

items.name: command-palette
items.title: Command palette
items.description: A searchable list of commands in a modal, opened with Cmd+K. Built on the native dialog.

props.name: commands
props.description: The commands to list and search. Each has an id, a label and an onSelect, and can have a group, keywords, a hint and an icon.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the palette is open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new open state when the palette should open or close, from the hotkey, Esc, a click outside or a chosen command.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder in the search field, also its accessible name.

props.name: hotkey
props.description: Open and close with Cmd+K / Ctrl+K.

props.name: labels
props.type: { oneResult?: string; results?: string; noResults?: string }
props.description: Visible text and screen reader text. Keys: `oneResult`, `results` (with `{count}`) and `noResults`, read out as the list changes.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the dialog.

a11y.text: Cmd+K or Ctrl+K toggles it unless hotkey is false. The dialog is a native modal dialog, so Esc closes it and focus stays inside. In the search field ArrowDown and ArrowUp move through the commands and wrap around, and Enter runs the active one and closes the palette. The field takes focus when the palette opens.

The dialog is labelled Command palette. The input is a combobox named by the placeholder text, with aria-controls, aria-autocomplete list and aria-activedescendant pointing at the active option, so focus stays in the field. aria-expanded is true only while there are results. A hidden status announces the count as you type (1 result, N results, No results), and the words come from labels. The results are a listbox labelled Commands with role option and aria-selected, and each group is labelled with its heading text. When nothing matches, the listbox is hidden and a No commands match message is shown. The search icon is aria-hidden.
Under reduced motion the opening animation is off.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.description: A panel that slides up from the bottom and can be dragged down to close.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the sheet is open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new open state when the sheet should close: the close button, Esc, a click outside or a drag down.

props.name: title
props.description: Accessible name, and the heading at the top of the sheet.

props.name: children
props.description: The content below the title.

props.name: labels
props.description: Visible text and screen reader text. Key: `close` (the name of the close button).

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the dialog.

a11y.text: Esc closes it, because it is a native modal dialog that traps focus and returns it to the opener on close. A visible 44 pixel Close button at the top right does the same with Enter or Space, and a click on the backdrop closes it too.
The dialog is labelled by title, which is also the h2 at the top. The Close button is named by labels.close. The grab handle is aria-hidden.
Under reduced motion the slide-in animation and the button transition are off.

Dragging the top area (handle and title) down by more than 30% of the sheet's height closes it, and a shorter drag springs back. The drag is an extra for pointer users: the Close button, Esc and a click on the backdrop do the same by keyboard.

items.name: rolling-number
items.title: Rolling number
items.description: A number whose changed digits roll up or down, read once by screen readers.

props.name: value
props.description: The number shown. Each digit rolls when it changes.

props.name: locale
props.description: Passed to Intl.NumberFormat, e.g. "da-DK". Leave it out for plain digits.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the inner span that holds the digits.

a11y.text: The full number is in one screen-reader-only span and read once. The rolling digits are aria-hidden.
The component is wrapped in MotionConfig with reducedMotion set to user, so Motion follows the system setting for the rolling digits.

items.name: rolling-number-demo
items.title: Rolling number demo
items.description: How to use Rolling number.

items.name: stepper
items.title: Stepper
items.description: A plus and minus counter with rolling digits that also works with the arrow keys.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value. Leave it out and the stepper keeps its own.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Starting value when the stepper is not controlled.

props.name: min
props.description: Lowest value; the minus button turns off there.

props.name: max
props.description: Highest value; the plus button turns off there.

props.name: step
props.description: Amount added or taken away per press.

props.name: label
props.description: Read aloud by screen readers, e.g. "Guests".

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value after each press.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer box around the buttons and value.

a11y.text: The number is a focusable spinbutton. ArrowUp and ArrowRight add step, ArrowDown and ArrowLeft subtract it, Home jumps to min and End to max. The values are clamped between min and max.

The spinbutton is named by the required label and sets aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax. The two buttons are named Fewer: <label> and More: <label>, and each is disabled at its limit. The icons are aria-hidden.
The buttons scale on press without a transition under reduced motion (motion-reduce), and the rolling number follows the system setting through Motion.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: An on and off switch whose knob stretches when pressed and springs across.

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled state.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Starting state when the switch is not controlled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new state each time the switch is flipped.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Turns the switch off for pointer and keyboard.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer span that wraps the switch and its label.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, linked to the switch. Pass this, `aria-label` or both.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Spoken name for screen readers. Required without a label; with one, it replaces the label when read aloud.

a11y.text: It is a native button with role switch, so Tab focuses it and Space or Enter flips it. It shows a focus ring and respects disabled.
The button sets aria-checked. The props type requires a name: either a visible label (a real label element tied to the button id) or an aria-label.
The component is wrapped in MotionConfig with reducedMotion set to user, so Motion follows the system setting for the knob.

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy button
items.description: Copies a value, and the icon and label roll over to say it worked, or that the browser said no.

props.name: value
props.description: The text that lands on the clipboard.

props.name: labels
props.type: { copy?: string; copied?: string; failed?: string }
props.description: Visible text and screen reader text for the idle, copied and failed states; defaults to English.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the button.

a11y.text: It is a native button, so Tab focuses it and Enter or Space copies.

The label sits in an aria-live polite span. It changes from Copy to Copied, or to Not copied when the browser refuses the clipboard, and returns after 1.8 seconds. The icons are aria-hidden. All three texts can be replaced with labels.
The component is wrapped in MotionConfig with reducedMotion set to user, so Motion follows the system setting for the icon and letter animation.

items.name: copy-button-demo
items.title: Copy button demo
items.description: How to use Copy button.

items.name: timed-undo
items.title: Timed undo
items.description: A delete button that counts down a few seconds and can be undone before anything happens.

props.name: seconds
props.description: Seconds the person has to change their mind.

props.name: label
props.description: Text on the button before it is pressed.

props.name: undoLabel
props.description: Text on the button while the countdown runs.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Runs when the countdown reaches zero without an undo.

props.name: onUndo
props.description: Called when the person undoes during the countdown.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the button.

a11y.text: One native button does both jobs. A press starts the countdown, and a second press during it undoes. onConfirm runs when the countdown reaches zero.

Once, when the countdown starts, a screen-reader-only polite live region says <label> in N seconds. Press again to undo. The counting number is aria-hidden, so it is not read every second. The button text changes from the label to undoLabel.

a11y.text: A full page: a promo line, a header with nav "Main" and a "Mobile" nav inside a details/summary, then main with the h1 in the hero and h2 sections (favourites, collections, story, reviews, FAQ, newsletter). Product names are h3 links, each collection is a link holding its h3, and the footer columns use h3.

Icon links carry an aria-label ("Search", "Bag, 2 items") and their icons are aria-hidden. Each product lists its colours as a list with the colour name in screen-reader-only text, followed by a visible count ("3 colours", labels.colours). Review stars are aria-hidden and quotes are figure, blockquote and figcaption.
"Add to bag" on each product card is a button that sits beside the product link, not inside it. Its name is "Add to bag: {product}", and it calls onAddToBag with the name and price.

The mobile menu and the FAQ are native details/summary, so Enter and Space open them. "Add to bag" is a native button that appears on card hover and on keyboard focus within the card. The newsletter field has a label, type=email and required, with a visible focus outline.

The hero entry transitions, the card lift, the image zoom, the "Add to bag" slide, the collection arrow nudge, the FAQ "+" rotation and the button press scale are dropped under reduced motion (motion-reduce).

Below the lg breakpoint the aside is hidden and the same nav, also named "Main", sits in a details menu.

The period switch is a fieldset with a screen-reader-only legend "Period" and native radios; only the chosen period's chart is shown. Each period is its own section named by its h2 ("Revenue, 7 days", "Revenue, 30 days" or "Revenue, 12 months"), so the name follows the chosen period.

The revenue bars are an ordered list named "Revenue by period, {period}", and each bar holds its value as real text.

Top products are an ordered list. The orders table sits in a focusable scroll region named "Orders table" (labels.ordersTable) so a narrow screen can scroll it by keyboard, and it has column headers; the status dot is aria-hidden and the status is written out. The charts are drawn inline here, not with bar-chart or sparkline.

The period radios and the mobile details menu use native keys. Each revenue chart is one Tab stop. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move between the bars, Home and End jump to the first and the last, and the active bar shows its tooltip. A hidden hint names the keys (labels.barsHint), and a status line reads the label and value of each bar you move to. The tooltip also shows on hover.

props.description: How `x` is written. Default: a plain number.

props.name: yFormat
props.description: How `y` is written, on the side axis too. Default: a plain number.

props.name: height
props.description: The plot's height in px. Default 280 below 560 px wide and 320 above (240/280 in compact density).

props.name: maxRadius
props.description: The largest bubble's radius in px. Default 40 (30 below 560 px wide, 22 below 400), and never more than an eighth of the height.

props.name: activeIndex
props.description: The bubble that is active (its tooltip shows), as an index into `data`, or null. Makes the selection controlled.

props.name: defaultActiveIndex

props.name: onActiveIndexChange

props.name: labels
props.description: Words for i18n.

props.name: density
props.description: "compact" makes the plot shorter. Inside a DataTile it follows the tile's density on its own.

a11y.text: The chart is one Tab stop. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, Home and End step through the bubbles: left to right on axes, largest first when packed. Any arrow with nothing picked goes to the first bubble. Escape lets go and closes a hover tooltip.
The chart is an image named by label and described by a hint. Each step is read once, and a hidden table holds the data.

items.name: lollipop
items.title: Lollipop
items.description: A ranked list with thin stems and round heads at each value: sort by value or name and the rows slide into place; one Tab stop with arrow keys, a tooltip per row, and the list itself is the data for screen readers.

props.name: data
props.description: One entry per row, in any order: `{ label, value, details? }`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the list shows, such as "Top merchants by spend, last 30 days". Names the list.

props.name: format
props.description: How values are written in the rows, the tooltip and on the axis.

props.name: sort
props.description: "value" puts the largest first, "label" sorts by name, "none" keeps the order of `data`. Default "value".

props.name: limit
props.description: Show only the largest n rows. Default all.

props.name: axis
props.description: Show the value ticks under the list. Default true.

props.name: activeIndex
props.description: The highlighted row (an index into `data`), or null for none. Pass it to control the highlight.

props.name: defaultActiveIndex
props.description: The highlighted row on first render when uncontrolled. Default null.

props.name: onActiveIndexChange
props.description: Called when the highlight moves by pointer, focus or keys, with null when it clears.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called when a row is clicked or pressed with Enter or Space, with its index into `data`.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show breathing skeleton rows instead of data.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in place of the rows when there is no data or every value is 0, such as a message and a next step.

props.name: labels
props.description: Words for other languages.

props.name: density
props.description: "compact" tightens the rows and columns. Inside a compact DataTile this happens on its own.

a11y.text: The list is one Tab stop with roving focus. ArrowUp and ArrowDown, Home and End move between rows; Escape lets go.
The list is named by label and each row is a button named like "1. Harbour Market: €289.20, Visits 6". The axis and tooltip are aria-hidden. While loading it is aria-busy with hidden loading text.
Under reduced motion the stems are at full length at once and rows jump instead of sliding. The loading skeleton pulses only when motion is allowed.

items.name: card-stack
items.title: Card stack
items.description: A fanned stack of payment or account cards: drag, flick, tap or key the front card away and the next comes forward, with its balance under the fan and dots to pick a card.

props.name: data
props.description: The cards, front first.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the stack, such as "Your cards".

props.name: format
props.description: The figure's format. Default two decimals; pass a currency for money.

props.name: value
props.description: The id of the card in front (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The card in front at first (uncontrolled). Default the first card.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new front card's id.

props.name: cardWidth
props.description: The widest a card gets, in px. Default 330, or 268 inside a compact tile.

props.name: renderCard
props.type: (card: StackCard, state: { front: boolean; index: number }) => ReactNode
props.description: Draw your own card face. The shell (fill, corners, shadow, motion) stays.

props.name: hideAmount
props.description: Hide the figure under the fan.

props.name: labels
props.description: Text overrides for the readout, buttons, hints and announcements, with English defaults.

a11y.text: The stack group is a Tab stop, and so are the buttons and the radio dots. ArrowRight and ArrowDown go to the next card, ArrowLeft and ArrowUp to the previous, Home and End to the first and last. Keys count only when the stack itself has focus. The dots are a radio group with roving focus. A tap (under 4 px), a drag past a threshold or a flick flies the front card off; a short drag does not.

A carousel group described by a hidden hint. Only the front card is a slide; the others are aria-hidden and inert. A switch by key, button or swipe is announced through a polite live region; the dots are not announced. The amount readout is aria-hidden, and hideAmount removes it.
Under reduced motion there is no fan-in, no flight and no rolling digits, and the button transitions are off.

items.name: transaction-list
items.title: Transaction list
items.description: Payments grouped by day with the day's net, signed amounts in tabular mono, incoming, pending and failed states that never rely on colour alone, and a show-more limit.

props.name: data
props.description: The payments. Days are sorted newest first; rows keep your order within a day.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the list, such as "Recent transactions".

props.name: today
props.description: "YYYY-MM-DD" of today, so the first days read "Today" and "Yesterday". Without it every day shows its date.

props.name: format
props.description: The amounts' format. Default two decimals; pass a currency for money.

props.name: categories
props.description: Colours per category name, such as { Groceries: 'var(--chart-1)' }.

props.name: limit
props.description: Show this many rows and put the rest behind "Show more". Default all.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Makes each row a button and is called with its payment.

props.name: selectedId
props.description: The id of the row that is open elsewhere, marked with the signal colour. Needs `onSelect`.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The level of the day headings. Default 4.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show placeholder rows while the data loads.

props.name: empty
props.description: What to show when there are no payments. Default a short line.

props.name: density
props.description: "compact" tightens the rows. Default follows the tile.

props.name: labels
props.description: Text overrides for day names, statuses, buttons and the spoken row, with English defaults.

a11y.text: With onSelect each row is a button, so Tab and Enter work, and the selected row has aria-current. Without onSelect the rows are plain list items. Show more is a button, shown when limit hides rows.

Each day is a group labelled by its heading, with a hidden "net" before the day total. A row is read as one sentence through visually hidden text and its visuals are aria-hidden. Pending, failed and incoming are shown by chip, glyph or struck-through amount as well as colour. Show more has aria-expanded and announces how many rows were revealed. Loading is a status region named by labels.loading.
Under reduced motion new rows appear at once and row transitions are off. The skeleton pulses only when motion is allowed.

items.name: week-schedule
items.title: Week schedule
items.description: A week by the hour with events in side-by-side lanes when they overlap, 44 px minimum blocks, a now line in the signal colour, and day tabs when the columns get too narrow.

props.name: data
props.description: The events of the week.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name, such as "This week".

props.name: weekStart
props.description: "YYYY-MM-DD" of the first column.

props.name: days
props.description: How many days to show. Default 7.

props.name: categories
props.description: The categories, in legend order. Without them events use their own `color` or the first series colour.

props.name: now
props.description: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM". Draws the now line when it falls inside the week and marks that day as today.

props.name: startHour
props.description: The first hour on the rail. Default 8.

props.name: endHour
props.description: The hour the grid ends. Default 21.

props.name: hourHeight
props.description: The height of an hour in px. Default 46, or 40 inside a compact tile.

props.name: layout
props.description: "auto" shows the week while each day gets `minDayWidth`, then day tabs. Default "auto".

props.name: minDayWidth
props.description: The narrowest a day column may get before "auto" switches to day tabs. Default 60.

props.name: day
props.description: The day shown in day tabs (controlled).

props.name: defaultDay
props.description: The day shown first in day tabs. Default today, else the first day.

props.name: onDayChange
props.description: Called with the day index when another day tab is chosen.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Makes each event a button and is called with it.

props.name: legend
props.description: Show the category legend under the grid. Default true.

props.name: locale
props.description: Number and date language. Default "en-GB".

props.name: labels
props.description: Text overrides for day names, counts, events and hints, with English defaults.

a11y.text: The schedule is one Tab stop. ArrowUp and ArrowDown move within a day, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight go to the nearest event on the next day that has events, Home and End go to the first and last event (of the day in narrow mode), and Escape closes the tooltip and, without onSelect, clears the active event. With onSelect the events are buttons with roving focus. In narrow mode the day tabs use ArrowLeft and ArrowRight with wrapping, Home and End.

Without onSelect a visually hidden hint describes the schedule (default "Use the arrow keys to move between events."). Each day is a list named by the day; events read like "Team sync, 14:30 to 15:30, Work". Without onSelect the active event is read through a polite live region; with onSelect focus moves to the event button. In narrow mode the days are tabs with a tabpanel. The hour rail, the week header row and the now line are aria-hidden.
Under reduced motion events appear in place at once.

items.title: Week schedule demo
items.description: How to use Week schedule.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A small label for tier, category, new and demo data: neutral, free, pro, new and demo variants that read in light and dark.

props.name: variant
props.description: What the label means, which sets how loud it is: - `neutral`: a category or any plain tag ("controls", "surfaces"), set in mono on a faint fill. The default. - `free`: free or open source ("Free", "MIT"), a hairline outline that steps back. - `pro`: the paid tier ("Pro"), inverted to the page's text colour, so it is the one label that stands out. - `new`: recently added ("New"), a raised key with a small success dot. The word carries the meaning, not the dot. - `demo`: marks example data ("Demo data"), a dashed outline, so made-up figures never pass for real ones.

props.name: children
props.description: The visible text. Keep it to a word or two.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the badge span.

a11y.text: Plain text in a span, not interactive. Pass an id and point a link's aria-describedby at it, so the tier is read with the link.

items.name: gallery-card
items.title: Gallery card
items.description: A catalogue card: a poster or a drawn fallback with the name, a loop video on hover or focus, the tier badge, category and new, and one link stretched over the card.

props.name: name
props.description: The item's name (a slug like "flux-image"). It is the link text and, without a poster, the poster.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the card leads. Always a real URL, so the card works without JS and opens in a new tab on Cmd/Ctrl click.

props.name: description
props.description: One or two sentences; clamped to two lines.

props.name: descriptionLang
props.description: The language of the description, when it differs from the page (e.g. English descriptions on a Danish page).

props.name: tier
props.description: Which tier badge to show.

props.name: category
props.description: A category label under the description, e.g. "surfaces".

props.name: isNew
props.description: Marks the item as recently added.

props.name: poster
props.description: Poster image (16:10). Decorative: the name is the link text. Without one, or if it fails, the card draws its own.

props.name: loop
props.description: A short muted video that loops on hover and focus. Fetched on first hover/focus; never plays under reduced motion.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Called on a plain click or Enter instead of navigating, e.g. to open a detail view. Modified clicks keep the link.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The heading level of the name.

props.name: labels
props.description: Every visible string, for other languages.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the card element.

a11y.text: One Tab stop per card: the name is the link and covers the card. Focus starts the loop like hover does. With onOpen, a plain click or Enter opens the detail view; Cmd, Ctrl and middle click keep the link.
The link is described by the tier badge and the description (aria-describedby). The video and the Enter hint are aria-hidden.
The loop never plays under reduced motion; the poster stays.

items.name: filter-bar
items.title: Filter bar
items.description: A tier switch (All, Free, Pro, New, with counts from props) and a scrolling row of category chips. Both are plain links, so it filters without JavaScript; with onChange it filters in place.

props.name: value
props.description: The current filter and category. Read it from the URL on the server so the bar renders right without JS.

props.name: counts
props.description: How many items each tier holds for the current category.

props.name: categories
props.description: The category chips in the order to show them, each with its count for the current tier (0 is fine).

props.name: allCount
props.description: The count on the "all" chip. Defaults to the sum of the category counts.

props.name: hrefFor
props.description: Builds the link for a state. Defaults to `?filter=<tier>&kat=<category>`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Filter in place: a plain click or Enter calls this instead of following the link.

props.name: shortcuts
props.description: Keys 1 to 4 pick a tier from anywhere on the page. Off: no keys, no hints, no aria-keyshortcuts.

props.name: labels
props.description: Every visible string, for other languages.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer wrapper.

a11y.text: Every tier and chip is a link in the Tab order. Keys 1 to 4 pick a tier; they are ignored while typing or when a modal is open, and shortcuts={false} removes them with their hints and aria-keyshortcuts. Focus stays on the chosen link.
Two labelled nav landmarks; the active link has aria-current. A polite status says what is shown. The chip scroller arrows are aria-hidden with tabIndex -1, since every chip is reachable by Tab.
The tier indicator slides with transform; under reduced motion it moves at once.

items.name: preview-stage
items.title: Preview stage
items.description: A measured preview frame: a width switch with a ruler and shutters, scale to fit, light and dark, reload and open in a new tab, plus loading and error states with try again.

props.name: title
props.description: Names the stage and the iframe ("data-tile demo").

props.name: src
props.description: A page to show in an iframe.

props.name: children
props.type: ReactNode | ((view: { width: number; theme: StageTheme }) => ReactNode)
props.description: Or your own content. As a function it gets the width and theme; plain nodes get the `dark` class in dark.

props.name: themeParam
props.description: Builds the iframe URL for a theme. By default it sets `mode=light|dark` in the query and keeps the rest.

props.name: widths
props.description: The widths to switch between, in CSS px.

props.name: width
props.description: The width, if you control it.

props.name: defaultWidth
props.description: The first width when you do not. Defaults to the widest.

props.name: onWidthChange
props.description: Called with the new width when a width is chosen.

props.name: theme
props.description: The content's theme, if you control it.

props.name: defaultTheme
props.description: The starting theme when the theme is not controlled.

props.name: onThemeChange
props.description: Called with the new theme when it is switched.

props.name: status
props.description: Drive the states yourself. Without it, an iframe is loading until it loads, and `children` are ready.

props.name: onReload
props.description: Called on Reload and Try again (the stage reloads its own iframe or remounts `children` either way).

props.name: timeout
props.description: Milliseconds an iframe may take, counted once it is in view, before the stage shows the error.

props.name: caption
props.description: A line beside the frame note, e.g. where the demo comes from.

props.name: height
props.description: The window's height. Defaults to clamp(300px, 48vh, 540px).

props.name: shortcuts
props.description: W and T while focus is in the stage. Off: no keys, no hints, no aria-keyshortcuts.

props.name: labels
props.description: Every visible and announced string, for other languages.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer group.

a11y.text: The width switch is a radio group with one Tab stop: arrow keys, Home and End move it. The theme control is a switch. W and T change width and theme only while focus is inside the stage, and shortcuts={false} turns them off. Try again moves focus to Reload.
The stage is a group named by title. A polite status announces width, theme, loading and error. Icon buttons have names; the ruler and shutters are aria-hidden.
The shutters and scale use transform; under reduced motion they jump to the end state. The loader shows only after 300 ms.

items.name: locked-code
items.title: Locked code
items.description: A locked Pro file: a blurred stub, an unlock link with the price, the facts, and the CLI and MCP commands to copy once you have a key.

props.name: name
props.description: The component's name, such as "flux-image". Used in the text and, with ".tsx", as the file name.

props.name: filename
props.description: The file name in the header. Default `${name}.tsx`.

props.name: stub
props.description: Placeholder lines drawn blurred behind the lock. They ship in the page's HTML, so never pass the real source: a few generic lines (imports, a props type, an empty function) are enough to read as code.

props.name: unlockHref
props.description: Where the unlock link goes, such as the pricing section.

props.name: onUnlock
props.description: Called when the unlock link is clicked, for opening a checkout in place. Call `preventDefault()` to stay.

props.name: price
props.description: The price after the unlock label, such as "€49". Leave it out for a plain "Unlock".

props.name: priceNote
props.description: One line under the link about the price, such as an introductory offer and when it ends.

props.name: facts
props.description: Short facts in a row under the price, such as "One-time payment".

props.name: commands
props.description: The commands that fetch the code with a key, each with a copy button. Leave it empty to drop the key row.

props.name: envVar
props.description: The environment variable the key lives in, shown in the key row.

props.name: setupHref
props.description: A page that explains how to set the key up, linked from the key row.

props.name: labels
props.description: Words for other languages.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The heading level of "The code is locked", to fit the page outline. Default 3.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the outer section.

a11y.text: Tab order: Unlock, How to set it up, Copy CLI, Copy MCP. The key slot lights on hover and on keyboard focus.

A region named by the file name and heading. The stub is aria-hidden: pass placeholder lines, never real source, since it ships in the HTML. Each command row is a group named after its command, so each Copy says what it copies.
No transition under reduced motion.

items.name: command-search
items.title: Command search
items.description: A search field that opens a Cmd+K palette on the native dialog, with grouped results, a preview pane for the active result, and a no-results state with suggestions.

props.name: items
props.description: Everything that can be found. Counts in the palette are taken from this list.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the chosen item after the palette has closed. Without it, the item's `href` is followed.

props.name: renderPreview
props.description: Your own preview for the active item, in place of the poster, title, description, badges and install line.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Searches to offer when nothing matches, shown with their hit counts (ones with no hits are left out, at most four). A function gets the query, for mapping words in another language. Default: the commonest categories.

props.name: shortcuts
props.description: Single-key shortcuts: "/" opens the search. Turn off for WCAG 2.1.4; Cmd/Ctrl+K keeps working. Default true.

props.name: hotkeys
props.description: Listen on the whole page for Cmd/Ctrl+K (and "/"). Turn off on a second search on the same page. Default true.

props.name: limit
props.description: Results per group while searching. Default 8.

props.name: initialLimit
props.description: Results per group with an empty field. Default 5.

props.name: open
props.description: Controls whether the palette is open. Leave it out to let the component keep track.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the palette starts open when it is not controlled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new open state when the palette opens or closes.

props.name: query
props.description: Controls the text in the field (the trigger and the palette share it).

props.name: defaultQuery
props.description: The starting text, such as `?q=` from the URL.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Called with the text each time the query changes.

props.name: action
props.description: Where the trigger form sends `?q=` without JavaScript. Default: the current page.

props.name: name
props.description: The query parameter's name. Default "q".

props.name: labels
props.description: Words for other languages.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the trigger field.

a11y.text: Cmd or Ctrl+K toggles it, and / opens it unless you are typing in a field or shortcuts={false}. Typing in the trigger opens it with the text. Arrow keys wrap, Home and End jump, Enter opens, Cmd+Enter copies the install line, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.

A modal native dialog with a combobox and a listbox; aria-activedescendant is set only when an option is active. Each group is role=group. The hit count is announced politely after typing stops, and the copy toast is a status.
Under reduced motion it opens and closes without animation; keyboard opens are always instant.
